title: Parquet reader hard cut and temporal acceptance
runbook_section: LIVE / Repair order and production gates

external_dependencies.for: The private Parquet API and bounded client are already integrated; this track receives only the unfinished d4 reader/capability scope.
The reader may cut coverage to availability only after the canonical schema, immutable-generation publisher and bootstrap receipt contract are frozen.

supersedes.parquet_duckdb_pivot_20260823:d4: The d4 reader/capability/browser scope is delegated here; the pivot keeps the private API and historical warehouse authority.

note: Hard-cut every eligible live map and tRPC reader to bounded day+bbox+zoom Parquet reads with explicit terminal states. Fire is first because production currently advertises Parquet capability while drawing through the legacy global PostgreSQL route.

shared_writes: src/lib/server/services/parquet-plane-client.ts and capability registries are serialized owners; no other track edits them until r2 lands.
gapless p0a owns the availability schema, publisher and bootstrap. Reader r2 receives the frozen artifact contract and owns only request-path consumption.
multiscale_polygon_surface_20260901 may consume the frozen support-geometry contract but may not race its reader implementation.
tripwires: Every time-bearing request includes settled day, viewport bbox and zoom/rung.
Published, governed_absence, day_not_written, lane_never_written and truncated remain distinct.
A browser abort must stop downstream work rather than only free the browser queue.
Legacy route removal requires parity evidence and an exact deployment rollback.
Capability reads may not list historical lane prefixes, open historical data parts, query PostgreSQL or invoke the one-time availability bootstrap.

slices.task: Freeze production request ownership and cold/warm timing evidence for every repointed surface; record fire route, TTFB, request-to-paint, response bytes, selected versus painted day, cache and cancellation behavior.
Hard-cut the fire map from useFireData and /api/fires to wildfire.getFireDetections with day, bbox and zoom; preserve explicit refusal/empty/truncation states.

Reconcile all tRPC reader and slider-capability ownership, latest/source-ceiling semantics and explicit Parquet response states without silent fallback. Replace request-time coverage listings with checksum-bound availability Parquet reads and fail closed when the artifact is absent or invalid.
Delete or quarantine the obsolete fire REST hook/route only after r1 parity, no-live-request evidence and rollback are recorded.
Run the focused reader/capability sweep, independent review and a deployment-safe evidence packet; do not perform the final production verdict owned by the fan-in acceptance track.
